title: Development comparison of state-content write interfaces
question: Can the current XOR-limited integrated PLM recover queried latent bits more reliably when the persistent-state write uses a residual transform rather than the single linear projection?
hypothesis: A residual state-write interface will improve queried-bit recovery and therefore improve development XOR accuracy without changing the encoder, CASM, optimizer, task distribution or held-out test sets.

endpoints.name: development_xor_q2_accuracy
endpoints.description: Mean XOR q2 accuracy on the registered development split.

decision_rule.condition: if an alternative write arm improves development XOR q2 accuracy over linear and does not violate integrity gates
decision_rule.licenses: select the best preregistered write interface for a later confirmatory test
decision_rule.does_not_license: general state-write superiority or any claim on E2E-006 held-out outcomes

decision_rule.condition: if no alternative improves the primary endpoint
decision_rule.licenses: retain the linear write interface and diagnose other state-content bottlenecks

held_constant: same optimizer, learning rate and weight decay
sealed E2E-005 and E2E-006 held-out compositions never used for selection
same evaluation episode objects across write arms within each seed
